newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends down sharply as specs, trade sell.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends down sharply as specs, trade sell.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures posted losses for the second day in a row Tuesday, slumping on a mixture of speculative and trade selling, dealers said.

Traders said a lack of follow through to the upside after last week's rally to more than one-month highs, coupled with the December contract's inability to breach the widely watched $1,400-mark, weighed on market sentiment.
"The market was on the defensive all day," one trader said. "Technicals dominated the action and technically, the market is looking a bit suspect."
When December failed to hold support near $1,370-$1,366 a tonne today, traders said speculators moved to relinquish their long positions.

Benchmark December delivery ended down $17 a tonne, to $1,360, after ranging between $1,371 and $1,358. Second-month March closed $15 lower, at $1,390, while the remaining months finished $13 to $15 weaker.
Despite today's steep losses, traders and analysts said the market continued to trade sideways without clear direction.
"I think the market is going to ratchet about the $1,300-$1,450 range," one analyst said.
"There is plenty of cocoa around," he added. "But there will be slightly less this year, so prices may go a little higher because the stocks to use ratio is going to decline."
Traders are hoping upcoming third quarter grind data, due out from the end of this week, may provide some fundamental impetus for the market.
Analysts expect strong third quarter Dutch, UK and Germany grind figures due to cool summer weather in much of Europe and a revival in chocolate demand in eastern Europe.
On the charts, traders pegged December support at $1,350, while near term resistance was seen at $1,375.
